title: Handle a key employee's resignation
summary: Review the resignation, applicable notice requirements and equity arrangements; agree a transition plan, arrange final pay and revoke access at the appropriate time. Record the exit and any continuing obligations under the applicable agreements and local rules.

parts.title: Take the resignation conversation properly: last day, transition shape, and whether a counter or a clean exit is honest

execution.rationale: The manager and employee discuss resignation remotely, agree the transition and last day, and record the outcome personally.

parts.title: Confirm the notice terms: the contract and handbook, plus whatever statute or collective agreement sets the minimum

geoResolutions.label: At-will is the baseline, so goodwill and the transition plan are the real levers
A week's statutory minimum notice after a month's service, with contracts usually setting more
Kündigungsfristen are statutory: §622 BGB sets four weeks to the 15th or month-end as the baseline, lengthening with tenure
geoResolutions.guidance: Termination and resignation require wet-ink written form (§623 BGB); the paper is law, not courtesy.

geoResolutions.label: The préavis comes from the convention collective more than the Code du travail; check your branch agreement
Notice runs off the employment contract and the state's Shops & Establishments Act
Resignation notice is statutory under the Código do Trabalho: 30 days up to two years of service, 60 days beyond
No statutory resignation schedule in most provinces; the contract and common-law reasonable notice govern, while federally regulated employers follow the Canada Labour Code
Apply the contract's notice period; when the contract is silent the Employment Act scale governs — 1 day under 26 weeks' service, up to 4 weeks after five years
Resignation notice comes from the modern award or the contract; the Fair Work Act s 117 minimums govern employer-initiated termination, so read the award clause first
One month of notice ends an open-ended employment; contracts can set more
geoResolutions.guidance: Under Civil Act Article 660 a termination notice takes effect one month after it reaches the other party. The resignation letter and the contract fix the actual last day, and final settlement of wages and severance then runs on the 14-day clocks (law rule kr.severance-pay).

geoResolutions.label: Notice runs on the contract with the Employment Ordinance floor: the agreed period but at least 7 days on a continuous contract, and 1 month where the contract is silent
geoResolutions.guidance: Employment Ordinance section 6 sets the notice floors, section 7 allows payment in lieu, and section 25 requires every sum due to be paid within 7 days after the termination date.

geoResolutions.label: At least 30 calendar days of notice ends an open-ended employment
geoResolutions.guidance: Employment Contracts Act § 98 sets the employee's ordinary-cancellation notice at no less than 30 calendar days; on the end date every claim from the relationship falls due (§ 84), and the employment-register termination entry follows within ten days (law rule ee.employment-register-before-work).

execution.rationale: The people lead and adviser review the employee's digital contract and handbook records before confirming the applicable notice terms.

parts.title: Run the equity math: vested vs unvested at the last day, and the plan's post-termination exercise window

execution.rationale: Calculate vesting and the proposed exercise-window record from the actual award terms and departure date.

parts.title: Put the exercise window in writing to the departing employee — a missed window is the classic post-exit dispute

geoResolutions.label: The plan's post-termination window plus the ISO 3-month rule set the deadline
geoResolutions.guidance: Plans commonly give 90 days, and ISOs lose their tax treatment if exercised more than 3 months after employment ends.

geoResolutions.label: EMI options carry their own post-cessation tax rules, so the written-window notice matters just as much

execution.rationale: Counsel and the equity owner check the actual award terms and send the individualized exercise-window notice through the employee's agreed digital correspondence channel.

parts.title: Plan the knowledge transfer: owned systems, in-flight work, credentials inventory, named successors

execution.rationale: Draft the handover map from supplied system ownership, in-flight work and credential inventories.

parts.title: Offboard on the last day: access revocation, device return, final pay on the timeline your jurisdiction sets

geoResolutions.label: Final pay on the state's required timeline (law rule us-ca.final-wages-timing for the California clock)
The exit paperwork is mandatory: solde de tout compte, certificat de travail, and the attestation France Travail
The full-and-final settlement timeline and gratuity after five years' service are the statutory tail

execution.rationale: The offboarding scope includes physical device return as well as digital access revocation and jurisdiction-specific final-pay administration.

parts.title: Run the exit interview — the honest 30 minutes that tells you why people actually leave

execution.rationale: A responsible interviewer holds the exit conversation remotely, listens and records the employee's account with appropriate confidentiality.

parts.title: Update the cap table, the org chart, and the on-call rotations

execution.rationale: The responsible administrators update the actual cap-table, organization and on-call systems and verify that the departure is reflected in each record.

metadata.trigger: A key employee resigns: notice is in hand and the transition starts now.
metadata.supportReason: The conversations (resignation, transition, exit interview) are irreducibly human; an agent can run the vesting math, draft the exercise-window notice, and execute the last-day offboarding checklist.

geoNotes.summary: Notice is statutory and contractual: a week's statutory minimum after a month's service, with contracts usually setting more — ACAS's notice-period guidance is the reference — and EMI options carry their own post-cessation tax rules, so the written-window step matters just as much.

Kündigungsfristen are statutory — §622 BGB sets four weeks to the 15th or month-end as the baseline, lengthening with tenure — and termination/resignation requires wet-ink written form (§623 BGB), so the paper is law, not courtesy.

The préavis comes from the convention collective more than the Code du travail — check your branch agreement — and the exit paperwork is mandatory: solde de tout compte, certificat de travail, and the attestation France Travail.

Notice runs off the employment contract and the state's Shops & Establishments Act; the full-and-final settlement timeline and gratuity after five years' service are the statutory tail — the labour ministry is the canonical starting point.

Resignation notice is statutory under the Código do Trabalho — 30 days up to two years of service, 60 days beyond — so the exit timeline is largely fixed by law; confirm equity-plan leaver terms and IP assignment on the way out.

No statutory resignation schedule in most provinces — the contract and common-law reasonable notice govern — while federally regulated employers follow the Canada Labour Code; the protective mechanics are the same offboarding checklist.

Notice is contractual, with the Employment Act's statutory scale as the floor when the contract is silent (1 day under 26 weeks' service up to 4 weeks after five years) — CPF runs through the notice period, and pass holders need the IR21 tax clearance before the final payment.

Resignation notice comes from the applicable modern award, enterprise agreement, or contract — the Fair Work Act 2009 s 117 minimums govern employer-initiated termination, not the employee's notice. Final pay and unused annual leave follow the award or agreement, and the end-employment checklist is the reference.

An open-ended employment ends one month after notice of termination reaches the other party (Civil Act Article 660); on separation, wages and all other amounts settle within 14 days (Labor Standards Act Article 36), plus severance for a year or more of service.

Notice is contractual with the Employment Ordinance floor: the agreed period but not less than 7 days on a continuous contract, and 1 month where the contract is silent (section 6); every sum due must be paid within 7 days after termination (section 25), and the IR56F/IR56G notifications to the Inland Revenue Department follow.

An employee's ordinary cancellation needs at least 30 calendar days' notice (Employment Contracts Act § 98), every claim from the relationship falls due when the contract ends (§ 84), and the termination is entered in the employment register within ten days (law rule ee.employment-register-before-work).

countryViews.title: Handle a key employee's resignation in United States
countryViews.summary: This is not the co-founder split; that is its own situation. This is the senior engineer or first AE handing in notice. Decide on the merits: counter, or accept a clean exit. Check what the contract and handbook say about notice, and what statute or collective agreement sets as the minimum; your real leverage is goodwill and a good transition plan. Run the equity math. Put the post-termination exercise window in writing to the departing employee; a missed window is the classic post-exit dispute, and the tax clock can be statutory (US plans commonly give 90 days, and ISOs lose their tax treatment if exercised more than 3 months after employment ends). Then knowledge transfer to named successors, same-day offboarding on the last day with final wages on the clock your jurisdiction sets (in California, due at quitting after 72 hours' notice, or within 72 hours of a no-notice quit; law rule us-ca.final-wages-timing, Labor Code §§ 202, 203), an exit interview that tells you why people actually leave, and the cap-table and rotation updates. Educational guidance, not legal or tax advice.
